sections.overview: The Icterine Warbler is a migratory Eurasian passerine that breeds across northern and eastern Europe and western Siberia, then winters in sub-Saharan Africa.
sections.identification: It has greenish upperparts, yellow underparts, a short pale wing panel and a slender, pointed-headed profile; it can be difficult to separate from the similar Melodious Warbler.
sections.habitat: For breeding it favours dense but discontinuous shrub cover in fresh, often moist places, including open woodland edges, river valleys, plantations and gardens.
sections.diet: It gleans insects from leaves and tall vegetation and may also catch prey in flight; the IUCN account notes that it takes fruit and berries in summer.
sections.behavior: Its trans-Saharan migration takes it to African wintering grounds mostly south of the equator.
sections.reproduction: It breeds in late spring and summer. A usual clutch contains four to five eggs.
sections.ecology: The Melodious Warbler H. polyglotta is its close congener and near-lookalike, but is more southerly; their songs and wing proportions help distinguish them where ranges meet.
sections.conservation: The global IUCN account lists the species as Least Concern. The French habitat account documents a long-term retreat from much of its former French range.
